chunks: From him, from Fudayla, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the broker who buys on commission, so silver is paid to him, and it is stipulated upon him that you bring what you buy, so take whatever you wish and leave whatever you wish. So he goes and buys, then the buyer comes and says: 'Take what you pleased and leave what you disliked.' He said: 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a broker to select goods on behalf of a buyer with a commission-based agreement?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of a discretionary brokerage model where the agent (simsar) purchases goods with cash on behalf of a principal, retaining the right to select or reject items before final confirmation. It highlights the flexibility in Shia commercial jurisprudence regarding agency (wakalah) and conditional sales, ensuring that the broker's discretion does not constitute uncertainty (gharar) as long as the principal ratifies the specific transaction. This ruling is foundational for understanding modern agency contracts and commodity trading in Islamic finance.
